const r = await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > docs/quality/summary-qa/scythe/2026-11-04-batch-231507/expanded-iteration-09/reader-a.json <<'EOF'
{
  "reader": "a",
  "inputs_read": [
    "summary-snapshot.md",
    "questions.json"
  ],
  "answers": [
    {"id":"Q01","answer":"Shuffle and place Factory cards face-down, selecting players + 1 and returning the rest unseen. Place one encounter token on each of 11 marked territories. Randomly choose one structure bonus tile and place it face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.","support":"supported","evidence":"Setup: 'number of players + 1'; '11 marked territories'; 'lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.'"},
    {"id":"Q02","answer":"On the map, put each character at its home base and two workers on the two land-adjoined territories adjoining that base. On the Faction Mat, place four mechs over abilities, six stars by the faction emblem, and leave one-time recruit spaces empty. On the Player Mat, place six technology cubes in green boxes marked with a black square, four structures in matching boxes, four recruits on bottom-row circles, and remaining six workers on Produce red rectangles; put the action token beside the mat ready for first placement. The Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw; the Player Mat sets starting popularity, coins and two objective cards.","support":"supported","evidence":"Setup, steps 3–4: Faction Mat sets 'starting power and combat-card draw'; Player Mat sets 'starting popularity, coins and objectives.'"},
    {"id":"Q03","answer":"You may take neither action after moving the token, so skipping both is allowed, but you must move to a different section from last turn. Rusviet may repeat a section, including Factory, but top and bottom actions each remain limited to once that turn. If taking both, take top before bottom; bottom first is prohibited. Top-row gains may pay the bottom-row cost. Pay all exposed red-box costs in full before the action; exposed green-box benefits may then be taken as much or as little as desired. Costs and benefits vary by mat and upgrades; use your mat.","support":"supported","evidence":"Turn Structure: 'optionally take'; 'bottom first is not allowed'; 'full cost'; 'as much or as little.'"},
    {"id":"Q04","answer":"An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls it and its resources. The enemy does not gain your structure's abilities; you keep those abilities even without control, except an uncontrolled Mill cannot produce. Pay action resources from any territories you currently control, even when acting elsewhere.","support":"supported","evidence":"Control, resources and home bases: 'enemy worker alone ... controls it'; 'Enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities'; resources from 'any territories you currently control.'"},
    {"id":"Q05","answer":"No: a normal unupgraded Move selects up to two different units, each moving one adjacent territory, and cannot select the same unit twice. A transported worker may subsequently move itself, or move onto a mech and be carried by its later move; carrying is not the worker's own movement. All units can carry any number of resources; only mechs can also carry any number of your workers, never your character.","support":"supported","evidence":"Move: 'two different units'; 'cannot use both selections to move the same unit twice'; carried worker may 'subsequently move itself.'"},
    {"id":"Q06","answer":"The Speed-enabled mech may enter, then must stop and cannot move again that turn; the enemy workers immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources. You lose one popularity per retreating worker, but insufficient popularity (including zero) does not prevent the retreat. Your workers cannot enter independently while enemy workers control the territory.","support":"supported","evidence":"Move, 'Enemy workers only': mech may enter but stops; workers 'immediately retreat'; insufficient popularity does not prevent retreat."},
    {"id":"Q07","answer":"After all units finish the Move action, resolve combats before the bottom-row action; the attacker chooses the order of multiple combats. Your workers cannot independently move into or out of territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.","support":"supported","evidence":"Move: 'Finish moving the other units, then resolve all combats before the bottom-row action; attacker chooses multiple-combat order.'"},
    {"id":"Q08","answer":"Bolster costs $1 and gives two power or one combat card, before upgrades; if the combat deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck, and if both deck and discard are empty, draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources (same or different) or one popularity, before upgrades. Put traded resources on a controlled territory containing at least one worker; if all your workers are at home, you cannot Trade for resources. Built Monument adds one popularity to Bolster; built Armory adds one power to Trade.","support":"supported","evidence":"Bolster and Trade sections specify $1 costs, choices, resource placement, worker condition and empty-deck rule."},
    {"id":"Q09","answer":"Pay all exposed Produce costs (power, popularity and/or coins) in full before producing; then choose up to two different controlled territories before upgrades, with each worker there producing one matching terrain token on that territory. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right and go in the producing village. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Workers exposed by production change future Produce costs, not the cost already paid.","support":"supported","evidence":"Produce steps 1–3: pay 'in full before production'; workers taken 'left to right'; new costs affect 'future' actions."},
    {"id":"Q10","answer":"Upgrade costs the number of oil tokens in its exposed cost boxes; move a technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box, improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost. Deploy costs the number of metal tokens in exposed Deploy cost boxes; place a chosen mech on a controlled territory containing your worker, never a lake. Its uncovered ability then applies to your character and every mech, not workers. The exact exposed costs vary by mat/upgrades. Even after completing all upgrades, mechs, structures and recruits, you may still pay for a bottom action to gain its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.","support":"supported","evidence":"Bottom-row actions: Upgrade—oil; Deploy—metal; completed bottom action may still be paid for coins and ongoing bonus."},
    {"id":"Q11","answer":"Build on a controlled territory with your worker; Factory is allowed, lakes and home bases are forbidden, and only one structure total may occupy a territory. Structures cannot move or be destroyed. A controlled Mill grants a bonus Produce territory; it can produce without an actual worker and each actual worker there also produces normally. If enemies occupy the Mill territory and you do not control it, the Mill cannot produce. Your Mine remains your personal tunnel for your units even when enemy-controlled; opponents cannot use its ability.","support":"supported","evidence":"Build: controlled territory with worker; structures cannot move/destroy. Mill works 'only while controlled'; Mine works 'even when enemy-controlled.'"},
    {"id":"Q12","answer":"Put the recruit permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus space on your Faction Mat, gaining two power, two coins, two popularity or two combat cards immediately; it cannot later move. Its ongoing bonus is set by the Player Mat circle uncovered when the recruit is removed: Upgrade +1 power, Deploy +1 coin, Build +1 popularity, Enlist +1 combat card. When active player and adjacent neighbors trigger it, resolve active player first, then left, then right, stopping if a sixth star ends the game. In two-player play the opponent triggers it once, not twice.","support":"supported","evidence":"Enlist and Ongoing recruits sections specify placement, one-time choices, action-linked bonus and order."},
    {"id":"Q13","answer":"Both combatants simultaneously and secretly choose dial power from zero to the smaller of seven and their current power, then may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech (even at zero dial); Rusviet People's Army adds one card if any workers are present. If both combatants have combat mech abilities, attacker uses theirs first, then defender. Reveal simultaneously and add dial and card values; attacker wins ties. Each pays the selected dial power from their Power Track; played cards are discarded face-up, and card values do not subtract extra track power.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat steps 1–4: 'simultaneously and secretly'; reveal simultaneously; 'attacker wins ties'; dial and card payment."},
    {"id":"Q14","answer":"Winner controls the territory and resources. All losing characters, mechs and workers retreat to their own home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy permits eligible units/carried workers to retreat to adjacent lakes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake; a winning defender loses none, and Polania Camaraderie has its stated aggressor combat exception. A non-Saxony winner with zero or one combat stars places one; at two it places none. Saxony places one after every victory while it has star tokens. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed any power on dial or through cards; a zero-total loser draws none.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat steps 5–6 specify retreats/resources, popularity, star limits and losing-player card reward."},
    {"id":"Q15","answer":"After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve the encounter if the character remains on the token territory. If contested entry is lost, the character retreats and the token stays. Gains go to the encounter territory. Pay the printed encounter cost only; no additional normal action costs or mat benefits, including ongoing recruit bonuses, apply.","support":"supported","evidence":"Encounters: resolve 'after the whole Move action and all combats'; contested loss leaves token; gains go to encounter territory; no normal costs/bonuses."},
    {"id":"Q16","answer":"Every player's character takes one Factory card on its first completed Move action there, after winning combat if necessary: look at the available cards, choose one, and return the rest. Each player gets at most one permanent card; later visits cannot exchange it. It acts as a fifth section with optional top then bottom and the usual no-repeat rule (Rusviet exception). Factory actions give no corresponding Player Mat coins, structure benefits or ongoing recruit bonuses. Factory bottom Move moves one unit up to two territories within that action, or three for a character/mech with Speed, subject to Mine access and normal movement/stops.","support":"supported","evidence":"Factory: 'Every player's character'; first finish of Move; one permanent card; bottom action movement and exclusions."},
    {"id":"Q17","answer":"Only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, may you reveal a completed objective; all requirements must be met at the moment of reveal. Place the objective star and put both objective cards on the bottom of their deck. Normally you score only one objective star. Saxony may complete both starting objectives, keeping the second card after the first is scored.","support":"supported","evidence":"Objectives and agreements: own turn timing, meet all requirements, both cards discarded; Saxony retains second."},
    {"id":"Q18","answer":"Stars are earned for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on the board, one revealed completed objective, a combat victory (up to two stars except Saxony's no-usual-limit rule), 18 popularity or 16 power. A placed star is permanent even if power or popularity later falls, and another player's stars never block a goal. The sixth star immediately ends play, with no equalizing turns or further actions.","support":"supported","evidence":"Stars and immediate end lists all goals and says stars are permanent, other players' stars never block, sixth ends immediately."},
    {"id":"Q19","answer":"If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, first collect its primary benefit, coins and your ongoing recruit benefit, then place the star. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that part of movement by returning initiating units to their prior territories; do not resolve another combat. For a neighbor recruit star, finish the active action and resolve active player first, then left neighbor, then right; if an earlier player placed the sixth star, later recruit stars/bonuses do not resolve.","support":"supported","evidence":"Sixth-star sequencing: bottom action benefit/coins/recruit first; pending battle undone; active/left/right order stops at sixth star."},
    {"id":"Q20","answer":"At 10 popularity (tier 7–12), each of 5 stars adds $4 = $20; 4 normal territories plus the Factory count as 7 territories (Factory counts three), at $3 each = $21; 13 controlled resources make 6 complete pairs at $2 each = $12. These categories add $53 to held coins, before the structure bonus. Your selected structure bonus scores from your structures even if enemies control their territories. Ties break by workers + mechs + structures (excluding character), then power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, and stars placed.","support":"supported","evidence":"Final fortune tier 7–12 rates; Factory counts 3; resource pairs rounded down; structure eligibility; tie order."},
    {"id":"Q21","answer":"A home base is not a territory. Normally you cannot move back into any home base, build there or deploy there; setup, forced retreats and Crimea's unlocked Wayfare are exceptions. Expansion bases without matching core factions are inactive placeholders.","support":"supported","evidence":"Control, resources and home bases: 'A home base is not a territory'; default prohibition and inactive expansion placeholders."},
    {"id":"Q22","answer":"Mountains produce metal, tundra oil, farms food, forests wood, and villages workers; lakes and the Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources. Resource tokens have no supply limit; use multipliers if needed.","support":"supported","evidence":"Produce terrain table; resources section says workers are not resources and no supply limit."},
    {"id":"Q23","answer":"All units may pick up, carry and drop any number of resources mid-movement; a mech may also pick up/drop any number of your workers, but cannot carry your character. Speed adds one territory of movement to each selected character/mech, not workers. A tunnel jump costs one movement step, with Speed's extra step usable before or after it; mech pickup/drop can occur mid-movement. Stops for enemy units and character encounters override Speed.","support":"supported","evidence":"Move: resource pickup/drop; Speed; tunnel jump; mid-movement carrying; stop overrides."},
    {"id":"Q24","answer":"Yes. Any unit may enter a territory occupied only by an enemy structure, taking control without combat. All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit.","support":"supported","evidence":"Move: 'Enemy structure only'; 'All printed tunnel territories are adjacent ... by any unit.'"},
    {"id":"Q25","answer":"You may not pay only part of a cost. If unable to afford any action, legally take a dead turn: move the token to a different section and take neither action. Since the previous section was Move, choose a different section.","support":"supported","evidence":"Turn Structure: 'Never pay only part of a cost'; dead turn by moving token to a different section and taking neither."},
    {"id":"Q26","answer":"A built Armory grants one power when you take Trade; a built Monument grants one popularity when you take Bolster. These bonuses trigger on those matching top actions. You retain structure abilities even without control, and enemy units do not gain them, so an enemy occupant does not take the benefit away; Mill is the stated control-dependent exception.","support":"supported","evidence":"Bolster/Trade benefits; control section says abilities persist except uncontrolled Mill; enemy units do not gain abilities."},
    {"id":"Q27","answer":"Riverwalk is a mech ability unlocked separately for all factions; it lets your character and all mechs, not workers, cross rivers onto faction-specific terrain: Nordic/Saxony forests and mountains; Rusviet farms and villages; Crimea farms and tundra; Polania villages and mountains. Nordic Swim is distinct: workers alone may cross rivers to land terrain, not lakes. It grants no lake movement to Nordic mechs; their lake movement comes from unlocked Seaworthy.","support":"supported","evidence":"Riverwalk table and note; Nordic Swim table; Seaworthy listed separately."},
    {"id":"Q28","answer":"Saxony Underpass makes controlled mountains and all tunnels, including your Mine, adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Rusviet Township makes controlled villages and the Factory adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Workers cannot use these shortcuts.","support":"supported","evidence":"Other unlocked mech abilities: Underpass and Township specify locations and character/mech Move actions."},
    {"id":"Q29","answer":"Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or your Mine and makes the opponent lose two power on the track, once per combat, not per unit. Nordic Artillery is also before combat and once per combat, not per unit, but its owner may pay one power to reduce the opponent's power by two.","support":"supported","evidence":"Underpass/Disarm and Seaworthy/Artillery entries specify timing, amount and frequency."},
    {"id":"Q30","answer":"Two mechs and three workers allow three combat cards total under Rusviet People's Army (one additional card total when any workers are present); workers alone never fight and a character or mech is still required.","support":"supported","evidence":"Rusviet People's Army: 'Two mechs and three workers allow three cards'; workers alone never fight."},
    {"id":"Q31","answer":"Crimea Wayfare lets its character/mechs move from a territory or home base to its own or any inactive faction home base regardless of distance, including inactive expansion bases. It cannot enter an active opponent's home base.","support":"supported","evidence":"Crimea Wayfare description specifies eligible bases and excludes active opponent base."},
    {"id":"Q32","answer":"Crimea Scout steals one random combat card from the opponent into your hand before combat, once per combat, not per unit. Crimea Coercion lets you spend one combat card as any one resource regardless of card value, once per turn.","support":"supported","evidence":"Crimea abilities: Scout and Coercion descriptions."},
    {"id":"Q33","answer":"Nordic Seaworthy lets character/mechs move to and from lakes and lets eligible units retreat to an adjacent lake instead of home; mechs may carry workers with them. Polania Submerge also allows character/mechs to move to/from lakes and additionally from any lake to any other lake, but gives no Nordic-style adjacent-lake retreat exception. With either lake ability, workers on lakes require a mech to move off, and carried workers and resources cannot be left behind on a lake when their carrier leaves.","support":"supported","evidence":"Seaworthy/Submerge descriptions and lake-carried-unit rule."},
    {"id":"Q34","answer":"Polania Camaraderie prevents popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after Polania wins combat as aggressor on its turn. It does not protect against popularity loss for driving off undefended workers without combat.","support":"supported","evidence":"Camaraderie entry explicitly states combat condition and excludes undefended-worker losses."},
    {"id":"Q35","answer":"Polania may choose up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order. Resolve the first gain before paying the second option's cost, so the first gain may pay that cost. The summary does not state a special rule requiring a specific number of options beyond 'up to two'; general encounter rules require a non-Meander faction to choose one affordable option.","support":"supported","evidence":"Polania Meander: 'up to two different options ... in either order; first gain can pay second cost.'"},
    {"id":"Q36","answer":"No. A character reaching an encounter token during Factory bottom Move stops and cannot move again that turn. The encounter is resolved only after the whole Move action and all combats, if the character remains there.","support":"supported","evidence":"Encounter and Factory rules: character stops; resolve after whole Move action/all combats; applies during Factory Move."},
    {"id":"Q37","answer":"Combat-card hand count is public, but card contents stay secret until revealed; during combat you may conceal whether you committed cards until reveal. Objective contents are secret until a completed objective is revealed. Coins are not hidden information, but you need not disclose their exact total value when asked.","support":"supported","evidence":"Public and hidden information table."},
    {"id":"Q38","answer":"Coins are the only tangible items exchangeable in informal agreements; agreements are unenforceable. In tournament play, even coin exchanges for deals/alliances are forbidden. A payment cannot cancel combat once moving units onto opposing units has initiated it; the combat must be fought, though bribes may influence the outcome.","support":"supported","evidence":"Objectives and agreements: coins only; unenforceable; initiated combat cannot be canceled."},
    {"id":"Q39","answer":"At popularity 0–6, score $3 per star, $2 per territory counted, and $1 per complete pair of controlled resources. At 7–12, score $4 per star, $3 per territory, and $2 per resource pair. At 13–18, score $5 per star, $4 per territory, and $3 per resource pair. Controlled lakes count; home bases do not. Resource pairs are rounded down, so a leftover single resource scores nothing.","support":"supported","evidence":"Final fortune table and text: controlled lakes count, home bases do not; resource income pairs rounded down."},
    {"id":"Q40","answer":"For adjacent-tunnel bonuses, count unique printed tunnel territories across all structures; Mines do not count as tunnels. Adjacent-encounter bonuses count unique printed encounter locations even after their tokens are removed. Adjacent-lake bonuses count unique lakes. Rivers do not break adjacency. For each category the payouts are 1 feature $2; 2–3 $4; 4–5 $6; and 6 features $9 for tunnels or 6–7 $9 for lakes/encounters; zero scores zero.","support":"supported","evidence":"Structure bonus table and note: unique features; encounter tokens may be removed; rivers do not break adjacency."},
    {"id":"Q41","answer":"Structures on tunnels count structures on printed tunnel territories, not Mines: 1 pays $2, 2 pays $4, 3–4 pays $6. Structures in a row count only your longest continuous straight line; rivers do not break the line; 1 pays $2, 2 $4, 3 $6, 4 $9. Structures on farms/tundras count qualifying structures combined; 1 pays $2, 2 $4, 3 $6, 4 $9.","support":"supported","evidence":"Structure bonus table: structures on tunnels, in a row, and on farms/tundras."},
    {"id":"Q42","answer":"Yes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat step 6 explicitly includes workers carried by defeated mech on a lake."},
    {"id":"Q43","answer":"No. A placed popularity star is permanent, but it does not protect current popularity; current popularity at final scoring determines the scoring tier. Another player's star never blocks a goal, so two factions can each star the same achievement.","support":"supported","evidence":"Stars are permanent despite later popularity drop; current popularity determines final scoring; other players' stars never block a goal."},
    {"id":"Q44","answer":"Randomly deal each player one Faction Mat and one Player Mat. Seat factions in board order clockwise: Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania, omitting inactive factions. This makes the immediate left and right neighbors relevant because their corresponding bottom-row actions can trigger ongoing recruit bonuses.","support":"supported","evidence":"Setup steps 2 and Ongoing recruits: board order; immediate left/right neighbors trigger bonuses."},
    {"id":"Q45","answer":"A river is a border between two land territories; a lake occupies an entire hex and extends to every adjacent shoreline. A unit with an applicable lake-movement ability may enter a lake from any surrounding land territory adjoining those shores.","support":"supported","evidence":"Move: river and lake definitions and lake entry from 'any surrounding land territory adjoining those shores.'"},
    {"id":"Q46","answer":"No, you may not keep a drawn encounter card private. Show it to all players, show its artwork, and read its capitalized thematic text aloud; you need not read every option aloud.","support":"supported","evidence":"Encounters: 'Show the encounter card to all players when drawn,' show artwork and read capitalized text aloud."},
    {"id":"Q47","answer":"There is no limit to the number of your friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.","support":"supported","evidence":"Control, resources and home bases: 'No limit applies to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.'"},
    {"id":"Q48","answer":"The next clockwise player may begin their turn after the current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action, while the current player decides which upgrade, mech, structure or recruit to gain.","support":"supported","evidence":"Turn Structure: next player may begin 'while the current player decides' which piece to gain."},
    {"id":"Q49","answer":"No. The chosen top action and bottom action are each limited to once within the turn, including for Rusviet. Rusviet's repeated section waives only the previous-turn section restriction.","support":"supported","evidence":"Turn Structure: top and bottom actions 'still each limited to once within the turn, including for Rusviet.'"},
    {"id":"Q50","answer":"You may gain $1 instead of moving units on the normal unupgraded Move action.","support":"supported","evidence":"Move OR coins: 'Alternatively gain $1.'"},
    {"id":"Q51","answer":"No. Workers never return to the Player Mat. The summary does not give an exception for workers that retreat; it states losing units retreat to home base, not to the Player Mat.","support":"supported","evidence":"Produce: 'Workers never return to the Player Mat'; combat retreats go to their home base."},
    {"id":"Q52","answer":"Yes. You may attack with zero power and/or zero popularity.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat: 'You may attack with zero power/popularity.'"},
    {"id":"Q53","answer":"Yes. You may still fight after reaching the non-Saxony combat-star limit; further victories at two combat stars award no additional combat star.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat: 'You may still fight after reaching your combat-star limit.'"},
    {"id":"Q54","answer":"A faction without Meander must choose one affordable option; it cannot decline to choose. It cannot select an unaffordable coin/popularity option. After choosing, it may take as little of the benefit as desired.","support":"supported","evidence":"Encounters: non-Meander 'must choose one affordable option'; may take as little benefit as desired."},
    {"id":"Q55","answer":"No. Combatants choose dial power simultaneously and secretly, not in turn order. They reveal simultaneously after optional cards are chosen.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat steps 1–3: 'simultaneously and secretly choose'; reveal simultaneously."},
    {"id":"Q56","answer":"Announce the bottom-row action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.","support":"supported","evidence":"Bottom-row actions: 'Announce the action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.'"},
    {"id":"Q57","answer":"No. Place a star as soon as you achieve its goal; the sixth star immediately ends play. An objective is different: you may wait to reveal a completed objective, but when revealing must meet all requirements at that moment and do so only on your own turn before or after an action.","support":"supported","evidence":"Stars: place as soon as achieved; Objectives: 'You may wait' to reveal a completed objective."},
    {"id":"Q58","answer":"Normally, none of your characters, mechs or workers may cross rivers or enter lakes; faction and mech abilities provide exceptions.","support":"supported","evidence":"Move: 'Units cannot normally cross rivers or enter lakes.'"},
    {"id":"Q59","answer":"No. The recruit is placed permanently on an open one-time bonus space and cannot later move.","support":"supported","evidence":"Enlist: 'It cannot later move.'"},
    {"id":"Q60","answer":"No. Only a character triggers an encounter; a mech or worker entering the territory does not resolve it or remove its token.","support":"supported","evidence":"Encounters: 'Only a character triggers an encounter.'"},
    {"id":"Q61","answer":"While you control the Mill territory, the Mill adds one bonus territory to your normal Produce allowance: two normal territories become up to three, or an upgraded allowance of three becomes up to four. The Mill itself counts as one producing worker and can produce even with no actual worker there, using its terrain's matching product; each actual worker there also produces normally, so their output is added rather than substituted.","support":"supported","evidence":"Produce: Mill bonus territory and allowance; Mill counts as one worker; actual workers produce additionally; works without actual worker."},
    {"id":"Q62","answer":"You control a territory if you have a unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit. Resources alone do not establish or preserve control; if your last unit leaves a territory where you have no structure, you do not control it.","support":"supported","evidence":"Control section defines control by unit or structure with no enemy unit."},
    {"id":"Q63","answer":"Build is paid with wood; Enlist is paid with food.","support":"supported","evidence":"Bottom-row resources: 'Upgrade oil; Deploy metal; Build wood; Enlist food.'"}
  ]
}
